questions.text: According to SPP 202 Section 5.2, MDPE is applicable only to what kind of work?

options.text: Non-creative work such as accounting, research, data gathering, and report preparation
All creative design services regardless of scope

rationale.a: SPP 202 Section 5.2 limits MDPE to non-creative work such as accounting, research, data gathering, and preparation of reports.
rationale.b: The source says MDPE does not account for creative work.
rationale.c: Percentage-of-PCC is a different compensation method.
rationale.d: The source is about Architect compensation, not contractor work.
rationale.correct: SPP 202 Section 5.2 limits MDPE to non-creative work such as accounting, research, data gathering, and preparation of reports.
rationale.takeaway: MDPE is effort/time based for measurable technical work.

questions.explanation: Includes office rent, which is overhead covered by the multiplier, not Direct Personnel Expense. Includes all firm staff, not just those directly assigned to the project; DPE only includes project-engaged personnel. Omits design architect, junior staff, and specialists; DPE includes all project team members regardless of level. DPE includes only salaries and labor-related benefits (PAGIBIG, PhilHealth, SSS) of architects, engineers, and technical staff directly engaged in the project's design and delivery. DPE = salaries + mandatory benefits (PAGIBIG, PhilHealth, SSS) for project-assigned staff only; office rent and overhead are in the multiplier, not DPE.

questions.text: What is the source-backed MDPE multiplier range in SPP 202?

rationale.a: The checked SPP range starts at 1.5 and extends to 2.5.
rationale.b: SPP 202 states that the MDPE multiplier ranges from 1.5 to 2.5.
rationale.c: Those values are above the checked SPP 202 range.
rationale.d: Those values are not in the checked source.
rationale.correct: SPP 202 states that the MDPE multiplier ranges from 1.5 to 2.5.
rationale.takeaway: Do not substitute broader practice ranges unless another verified source is attached.

questions.text: What does M represent in the MDPE formula?

options.text: Multiplier to account for overhead and reasonable profit

rationale.a: Mobilization is a payment concept in a different source.
rationale.b: The formula defines M as the multiplier used to account for overhead and reasonable profit.
rationale.c: Materials cost belongs to PCC, not M.
rationale.d: Construction progress is not the formula variable M.
rationale.correct: The formula defines M as the multiplier used to account for overhead and reasonable profit.
rationale.takeaway: M is applied after direct technical cost is identified.

questions.text: Which sequence matches the SPP 202 MDPE computation?

options.text: PCC x percentage, then add land cost
Direct cost x M, then add reimbursable expenses R
R x M, then subtract direct cost
Architect fee plus consultant fee equals PCC

rationale.a: That describes a different percentage-of-PCC approach.
rationale.b: SPP 202 states Fee = Direct Cost x M and Total Cost of Service charged to Client = Fee + R.
rationale.c: The source adds R after Fee, not before multiplying R.
rationale.correct: SPP 202 states Fee = Direct Cost x M and Total Cost of Service charged to Client = Fee + R.
rationale.takeaway: Compute direct cost, multiply by M, then add reimbursables.

questions.text: Which variable group represents hours spent by the Architect, consultants, and technical staff?

rationale.a: A, C, and T are hourly rates, not hour counts.
rationale.b: The formula defines AN, CN, and TN as the number of hours spent by the Architect, consultants, and technical staff.
rationale.c: M is the multiplier and R is reimbursables.
rationale.d: PCC and FPCC are construction-cost concepts.
rationale.correct: The formula defines AN, CN, and TN as the number of hours spent by the Architect, consultants, and technical staff.
rationale.takeaway: Separate rate variables from hour-count variables.

questions.text: Which item is a source-backed reimbursable example under MDPE?

options.text: Transportation or per diem for assigned personnel beyond the stated distance condition

rationale.a: SPP 202 lists transportation, housing/living allowance, per diem, extra printing, calls, technical tests, licenses, fees, taxes, and similar project cost items as reimbursables.
rationale.b: The Architect fee is the result of the computation, not a reimbursable example.
rationale.c: Land acquisition cost is not listed as an MDPE reimbursable.
rationale.d: The checked source does not state a fixed contingency.
rationale.correct: SPP 202 lists transportation, housing/living allowance, per diem, extra printing, calls, technical tests, licenses, fees, taxes, and similar project cost items as reimbursables.
rationale.takeaway: R is added after Fee in the source formula.

questions.text: Why does the source say MDPE does not account for creative design work?

options.text: Because creative design value cannot be measured merely by time spent
Because creative design has no professional value
Because creative design is always free
Because PCC includes all design fees

rationale.a: SPP 202 says the value of creative design cannot be measured by the length of time spent on the work.
rationale.b: The source values creative work but says time alone cannot measure it.
rationale.c: The source does not say creative design is free.
rationale.correct: SPP 202 says the value of creative design cannot be measured by the length of time spent on the work.
rationale.takeaway: This is why MDPE is confined to measurable non-creative work in the checked source.

questions.text: If direct cost is PHP 1,200,000 and M is 2.5 with no reimbursables stated, what is the Fee before R?

rationale.c: Fee = Direct Cost x M, so PHP 1,200,000 x 2.5 = PHP 3,000,000.
rationale.correct: Fee = Direct Cost x M, so PHP 1,200,000 x 2.5 = PHP 3,000,000.
rationale.takeaway: Only add R if reimbursable expenses are given.

questions.text: Before agreeing on MDPE, what should the Architect make known to the Client?

options.text: The rates of professionals/personnel assigned and the multiplier to be applied
Only the final contractor bid price
Only the Owner land acquisition cost

rationale.a: SPP 202 says the Architect shall make known the rates of professionals/personnel assigned and the multiplier before agreeing on MDPE.
rationale.b: Contractor bid price is not the MDPE disclosure item stated here.
rationale.d: The source does not provide guaranteed accuracy bands.
rationale.correct: SPP 202 says the Architect shall make known the rates of professionals/personnel assigned and the multiplier before agreeing on MDPE.
rationale.takeaway: MDPE depends on transparent rates, hours, multiplier, and reimbursables.

Total Cost of Service equals Fee plus R
The normal MDPE range is 2.8 to 3.5 for complex projects

rationale.d: The checked SPP 202 source supports a multiplier range of 1.5 to 2.5, not 2.8 to 3.5.
rationale.correct: The checked SPP 202 source supports a multiplier range of 1.5 to 2.5, not 2.8 to 3.5.
rationale.takeaway: Stay inside the audited local source range.
